title: Honey Locust: Old Honey Locusts You Can Visit
meta_description: Wild honey locusts carry branched thorns up to fifteen centimetres long. Three mapped, in Florence, Copenhagen and Zaragoza.
intro: A wild honey locust is armed. Branched thorns up to fifteen centimetres long grow straight out of the trunk and the older wood, generally read as a defence against browsing animals that no longer exist in North America. Street plantings use thornless varieties, which is part of why the three here look so different from one another. Zaragoza's had three main branches taken out of it at some point and came out the far side as a parasol, a flat horizontal crown on a short trunk. Florence's has never been bred for anything: five and a half metres round, standing alone at a residential junction, and known locally as Spino di Giuda, which people regularly confuse with the pink flowered tree of the same legend. Copenhagen's has been surveyed and remeasured since 1941, twelve metres then and sixteen in 2019.
